cells.tense: Something you carried the whole way is standing finished behind you, and you're clear about what it took.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you've finished to someone today with nothing asked back — say only what it took to get it done, and leave it with them whether they take it up or not.
cells.core:
By now there's something behind you that stands up on its own, and you know the days it took to get there — the ones you kept going and the ones you didn't. It got finished because you stayed pointed at it, and you're holding the plain fact of that.

What's here now is a choice about what the next stretch of effort is for — which one you aim at, and whether the aim comes from clear ground or from the leftover press of the last thing. Handing one finished piece to someone without needing a verdict on it opens the ordinary sound of it and a little room where the next decision can move.
cells.sheetLine: You carried it through to standing, and you know what it took.
cells.verb: carry a thing all the way through to where it stands finished
cells.place: the part of you that keeps moving toward what it has decided on

cells.tense: You're already running the next one before the last one has landed, and the aim is set further out than today.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that isn't finished yet and do nothing on it today that a camera couldn't see — no planning it, no checking the numbers, no saying it out loud — and let the day hold it.
cells.core:
You can hold a direction through resistance without it eating you, and on an ordinary day that looks like steady, unhurried work on the thing in front of you, one piece at a time.

This is the version where the finishing keeps getting pushed out because the next one is already underway, and then the one after that. The aim stays out past today, and the drive does its job so hard there's no open space left for anything to land in. Holding off on one unfinished thing for a day leaves a gap where something can come in that isn't yours to plan.
cells.sheetLine: You're working the next thing before the last one has landed.

cells.tense: There's a finished thing behind you that you're not standing on, and the next aim hasn't come.
cells.ask: Name one thing you finished out loud, in your own words, at the table you're at — say it plainly and stop, without counting up anything about it.
cells.core:
When this part is on track, you pick a direction and stay pointed at it, and the days add up to something you'd recognize as done. That's ordinary here, it doesn't need a fire under you, and the finished thing gets its moment of standing before you turn to the next.

As it stands, the momentum has gone still. The finished thing back there isn't something you're treating as yours, and with nothing to point at, the smallest motion starts to feel like the wrong move. Naming one done thing plainly and out loud gives the floor back where the push used to start from.
cells.sheetLine: Something you finished got set down and stayed down.

cells.place: the part of you that keeps moving toward what it has decided on

cells.tense: You're still driving — still picking the next direction and moving — but you describe it as just how things are.
cells.ask: Write down one choice that's still open — what to start, what to drop, where this year's effort goes — with your own answer on one plain line, and leave the note where you'll see it, whether or not you act on it.
cells.core:
Directing effort toward a goal is something you can do on a normal day — decide, aim, keep at it — and you'd call that getting on with it. The schedule gets made, the work gets pointed somewhere, and nobody has to announce it.

All the same, you're choosing direction most days and talking about it as though the schedule chose, or the family expects, or there's simply no other way. The momentum is running; your hand on it isn't admitted. Putting one open choice down in your own words, with your own answer beside it, is a claim you can point to later — the plain fact of having decided, on paper.
cells.sheetLine: You're picking the direction and calling it just how things are.

attempts.check: The record supports only the mechanism — a completed material cycle in a life, and in against/behind/disowned relationship to it. Nothing supports a claim about why this person is where they are, what it cost them, or what they'd feel on doing the ask; so each cell describes what the capacity itself is doing, in a moment they could check. The likely objection is that a finished thing may not be theirs at all — a job, a house, a debt paid off in a family — so the cells name finishing and carrying-through in plain terms and leave the content of it open. The ask in each cell is a thing a camera could watch them do today and teaches them something even if the tense is wrong about them; the sentence that would serve the writer more than the reader is any that certifies the person's strength, which is why none of them praise.
